summary: This Dockerfile creates a Docker image for running Cypress tests (an automated testing tool). It starts with a pre-built Cypress image, sets up a non-root user account for security, installs project dependencies, copies test files into the image, verifies the Cypress installation, and configures the container to run tests in Chrome by default.

explanations.3: ARG creates a build-time variable that can be passed in when building the image; USER_ID=1000 sets a default value but allows it to be overridden.
explanations.13: These ARG lines re-declare the variables so they're available in this stage of the build; Docker build stages don't automatically inherit ARG values without re-declaration.
explanations.18: This creates a new user group and a new user account with specific numeric IDs and adds that user to the 'node' group so it has permissions to run Node.js tools.
explanations.24: This switches the Docker container to run as the non-root user we just created, which is a security best practice.
explanations.27: COPY with --chown changes ownership of the copied files to our user in one step; package*.json matches both package.json and package-lock.json (the asterisk is a wildcard).
explanations.40: CMD specifies the default command to run when the container starts; this will execute Cypress tests in headless Chrome mode.
